name: Coverage Atlas learned selection rules - round 1
learned_preferences: Live tracks do not count toward coverage.
Snippets, excerpts, callout hooks, and similar promo fragments do not count.
Ordinary remixes do not count toward coverage.
A remix with an additional featured artist counts as unique content.
Versions and non-live acoustic variants count as songs/variants.
The same artist/title is considered the same song even when duration differs slightly.
Prefer a release whose valuable-track set strictly contains the other's.
If valuable coverage is identical, prefer the release with fewer total tracks/files.

Tracks inside release folders explicitly labeled Snippet, Excerpt, Preview, Callout, or Hook are promotional fragments even when the individual track titles omit those labels. A generic Sampler folder alone does not imply snippets.

When valuable track coverage, raw track identities, track count, and CD media type are equivalent, prefer the rip with the higher Logchecker score; if either score is unavailable or tied, do not decide by this rule.

Dynamic range is not a normal selection rule. In default mode it is measured only after all ordinary rules fail and only for strict absolute duplicates; CD duplicates also require equal Logchecker scores. DR priority mode is an explicit override handled by the Reasoning Lab itself.

If two releases have byte-identical rip-log contents and identical audio-file signatures, they are treated as a copied duplicate. Keep exactly one copy; prefer the release/log naming that does not look like a duplicate suffix such as (1) or Copy, otherwise use a stable path order.

If two releases preserve the same valuable coverage and every difference between them is an ignored remix/live/snippet track, they are equivalent for selection. Do not ask the user; keep one deterministic canonical release.
